    17  /**
    18   * @brief Represents a decoded, structured text value.
    19   *
    20   * vCard defines structured values for properties such as N
    21   * and ADR. These values consist of "components", where each
    22   * component may contain multiple values.
    23   *
    24   * To avoid confusion with existing libical terminology, the
    25   * vcardstructuredtype uses the term "field" to refer to a
    26   * "component". A vcardstructuredtype consists of zero or more
    27   * fields, each of which consists of zero or more values.
    28   * A field is represented by a vcardstrarray. A field of value
    29   * NULL is treated equally to an empty vcardstrarray.
    30   *
    31   * @par Ownership
    32   * A vcardstructuredtype is reference counted, but its fields
    33   * are not. Callers may read and alter the contents of fields,
    34   * but they must not free a field other than by calling
    35   * vcardstructured_set_field_at() with a NULL field value.
    36   */
    37  typedef struct vcardstructuredtype_impl vcardstructuredtype;
    38
    39  /**
    40   * @brief Creates a new instance of vcardstructuredtype.
    41   * @param num_fields The initial number of fields.
    42   * @sa vcardstructuredtype_unref()
    43   *
    44   * @par Ownership
    45   * The returned value has refcount 1. It is the caller's responsibility
    46   * to call vcardstructuredtype_unref() after it's no longer used.
    47   */
    48  LIBICAL_VCARD_EXPORT vcardstructuredtype *vcardstructured_new(size_t num_fields);

    55   * @par Ownership

    58   */
